fixes.explanation: I get it, a crown is a big thing to ask for. But in this cave prayer, David doesn't mention a crown at all. He lifts his voice "for mercy" (Psalm 142:1). I know a little about being stuck, since I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and a hat wasn't on my mind there either.

Nope, it's the opposite. David says, "I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him." (Psalm 142:2). He reveals his trouble to the LORD, so he isn't hiding it from Him. That's why this one is False.

False is right. David says, "I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him." (Psalm 142:2). He reveals his trouble to the LORD instead of hiding it. I think that's a pretty honest way to pray.
A snare, yes. David says, "Along the path I travel they have hidden a snare for me." (Psalm 142:3). A snare is a trap. And he tells us it was hidden along his path.

Close in spirit, but that's not the word. David says "…they have hidden a snare for me." (Psalm 142:3). A spear and a snare are two different things. A snare is a trap, and David says it was hidden along his path.
That's it. David says, "Look to my right and see; no one attends to me." (Psalm 142:4). He tells the LORD to look, and what he says is that no one attends to him. I think that sounds lonely.

Not in this psalm, friend. David says, "Look to my right and see; no one attends to me." (Psalm 142:4). He doesn't name a friend there, only that no one attends to him. I think that's what makes the cave feel so empty.

His mighty men aren't named in this prayer. David says, "Look to my right and see; no one attends to me." (Psalm 142:4). So what he tells the LORD is that no one is attending to him. That's the whole point of what he's saying.

I see the thought, but that's not the word David uses. He says, "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living." (Psalm 142:5). Right after saying no one cares for his soul, he turns to the LORD and calls Him his refuge. A refuge is a safe place to run to.
The deep sea isn't in this psalm. David asks, "Free my soul from prison…" (Psalm 142:7). I think that word pictures being shut in. The ocean never comes up.

I can see the dry and lonely feeling, but that's not the word. David asks, "Free my soul from prison…" (Psalm 142:7). I think he's picturing being shut in, not wandering around outside. I bet he wants the LORD to open the door.

David does ask to be rescued from his pursuers (Psalm 142:6). But the ones he says will gather are someone else. He says, "The righteous will gather around me because of Your goodness to me." (Psalm 142:7).
